name: French Rolls
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: butter and lard, mixed in equal proportions
ingredients.originalText: one cup of butter and lard, mixed in equal proportions

ingredients.name: one-half cup of good yeast, or half a cake of compressed yeast
ingredients.originalText: one-half cup of good yeast, or half a cake of compressed yeast

instructions.text: Add flour enough to make a stiff dough
In the morning, add two well-beaten eggs
Knead thoroughly and let it rise again
With the hands, make it into balls as large as an egg
Roll between the hands to make long rolls (about three inches)
Place close together in even rows on well-buttered pans
Cover and let them rise again
Bake in a quick oven to a delicate brown

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Add flour enough to make a stiff dough
2. Let it rise over night
3. In the morning, add two well-beaten eggs
4. Knead thoroughly and let it rise again
5. With the hands, make it into balls as large as an egg
6. Roll between the hands to make long rolls (about three inches)
7. Place close together in even rows on well-buttered pans
8. Cover and let them rise again
9. Bake in a quick oven to a delicate brown
